Leave a Neutral or Negative Review (If You Haven’t Already)** - Since you didn’t actually leave a review, you can now **leave a truthful but critical review** (e.g., *"Received a free item without leaving a review—this is against Amazon’s policies."*). - This adds **public pressure** and makes it harder for them to continue the practice. #### **3. Consider Reporting to the FTC (If You Want to Go Further)** - If this seller has a pattern of fake reviews (which they likely do), you could file a complaint with the **Federal Trade Commission (FTC)** at [reportfraud.ftc.gov](https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/). While Amazon is the primary target here, the FTC may investigate if this is part of a larger scam. #### **5. Warn Other Buyers (Anonymously)** - If you’re comfortable, you could leave a **warning in the comments section** of their listings (e.g., *"This seller offers free items for reviews—don’t fall for it!"*). - This doesn’t violate Amazon’s rules but helps others avoid the same issue. --- ### **Why Not Just Ignore It?** - **They’re Likely Doing It to Many Others** – If they’ve been doing this for years with 100% ratings, they’ve probably manipulated thousands of reviews. Reporting helps Amazon catch them. - **Amazon’s Algorithms Are Getting Smarter** – If enough buyers report them, Amazon may **suspend their account**, which would hurt their business. - **You Got a Free Item—But at What Cost?** – While you benefited once, you’re supporting a seller who **misleads customers**, which can lead to **higher prices for everyone** (since fake reviews make their products seem more popular than they are). --- ### **Final Verdict: Yes, You Should Report Them** But **don’t just report them—take a multi-step approach** to maximize the impact. This way, you’re not just protecting yourself but also helping Amazon and other buyers from being scammed. Would you like help drafting the exact report message to Amazon?
